prompts.applies:
You get ONE requirement of a software system, and a statement B about ONE snapshot of that system. B is not given: it may be true or false, and you have to say which. B is written as a fact marked TRUE or FALSE; B marked FALSE says that the fact is not the case.

Only some situations count: those in which the condition of the requirement is the case (what comes after WHEN, WHILE or IF; a requirement without such a part has no condition, and every situation counts), and in which the system has done everything the requirement demands, with its words read exactly as written. A situation in which the condition is not the case does not count, although the requirement is not broken in it. Must B be true in every situation that counts? Answer:
- yes: by the meaning of the requirement's words alone, B is true in every situation that counts (if it demands that a letter was answered, a letter was received; if it demands that every window is shut, the kitchen window is shut).
- no: there can be a situation that counts in which B is false. Look for one before you answer. This is also the answer when B would usually come before what the requirement demands, or when a system would need B to bring it about. Do not assume how the system works, or that anything succeeds (if it demands that the gate is open, nobody need have opened it today; if it demands that the bell is rung once, the bell need not have been heard).
- unclear: the words can reasonably be read both ways.

First give the reason in one or two sentences, then the answer. If the answer is yes, also write what connects the two as one plain sentence ("A letter that was answered was received."); otherwise leave "fact" empty.

If the answer is yes, say in "by" what makes B true. "condition": B is true as soon as the condition of the requirement is the case, whatever the system then does (the condition is that a letter is sent back, and B says that a letter arrived). "demand": it takes what the requirement demands (it demands that a letter was answered, and B says that a letter was received). If the answer is not yes, write "none".
